title: Billing kit: rounding, proration, tiers, taxes and invoices
statement:
# Billing kit (`src/`)

Five billing modules, all with amounts in **integer cents**: `money.mjs`, `proration.mjs`, `tiers.mjs`, `tax.mjs` and `invoice.mjs` (`proration` and `tax` use `divRound` from `money`). Users report that refunds (negative amounts) are not rounded like the equivalent charges and that a package with a quantity exactly equal to a tier's limit is charged at the price of the next tier. All modules must fully obey the contract below; fix whatever is necessary without changing the API.

## `src/money.mjs`

- `ROUNDING_MODES` = `['half-even', 'half-up', 'floor', 'ceil', 'trunc']`.
- `divRound(n, d, mode = 'half-even')`: quotient of `n / d` (safe integers) rounded to an integer:
  - `'half-even'`: nearest integer; a tie (fractional part exactly ½) goes to the **even** one;
  - `'half-up'`: nearest integer; a tie goes **away from zero**;
  - `'floor'`: toward −∞; `'ceil'`: toward +∞; `'trunc'`: toward zero.
  - It is the exact value of `n / d` that is rounded: the modes apply equally to negative quotients (half-even/half-up are symmetric with respect to zero). `d` may be negative. The result is never `-0` (returns `0`).
  - `n` or `d` not safe integers, `d === 0` or unknown mode → `RangeError`.
  - `divRound(25, 10)` → `2`; `divRound(35, 10)` → `4`; `divRound(-35, 10)` → `-4`; `divRound(-25, 10, 'floor')` → `-3`; `divRound(-1, 3, 'ceil')` → `0`.
- `applyRate(cents, rateBp, mode = 'half-even')` = `divRound(cents × rateBp, 10000, mode)` (`rateBp` in basis points: 250 = 2.5%). Non-integer arguments or a product outside `Number.isSafeInteger` → `RangeError`. E.g.: `applyRate(1050, 250)` → `26`; `applyRate(5, 5000)` → `2`.
- `sumCents(values)`: sum; an item that is not a safe integer → `RangeError`; `[]` → `0`.
- `fromDecimal(text, mode = 'half-even')`: `[spaces][+|-]digits[.digits][spaces]` (decimal point, any number of decimal places) → cents; places beyond the second are rounded with `divRound` in the given `mode` (on the signed value). Invalid format → `SyntaxError`. E.g.: `'12.5'` → `1250`; `'0.125'` → `12`; `'0.135'` → `14`; `'-0'` → `0`.
- `toDecimal(cents)`: `1250` → `'12.50'`, `-5` → `'-0.05'`, `0` → `'0.00'`, `123456` → `'1234.56'` (no thousands separator).

## `src/proration.mjs`

Dates are `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings in the **proleptic Gregorian** calendar (leap year: divisible by 4, except those divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400), without time zone. Intervals `{ start, end }` are half-open `[start, end)`.

- `isLeapYear(y)`, `daysInMonth(y, m)` (m from 1 to 12).
- `parseDate(text)` → `{ y, m, d }`; requires exactly `4-2-2` digits and an existing date, otherwise `RangeError` (`'2023-02-29'`, `'2024-1-01'`, `'2024-04-31'`). `formatDate({ y, m, d })` does the inverse.
- `dayNumber(text)`: days since `1970-01-01` (which is `0`; `1969-12-31` is `-1`); `fromDayNumber(n)` is the inverse. `addDays(text, n)` and `daysBetween(a, b)` = `dayNumber(b) − dayNumber(a)` derive from them. E.g.: `dayNumber('2000-03-01')` → `11017`; `daysBetween('1999-01-01', '2001-01-01')` → `731`.
- `prorate(amountCents, period, usage)`: `overlap = max(0, min(endP, endU) − max(startP, startU))` in days; result `divRound(amountCents × overlap, periodDays)` (half-even). Period with `end <= start` or usage with `end < start` → `RangeError` (usage with `start === end` is valid and gives `0`).
  - `prorate(3000, { start: '2024-04-01', end: '2024-05-01' }, { start: '2024-04-16', end: '2024-06-01' })` → `1500`.
  - `prorate(5, { start: '2024-01-01', end: '2024-01-03' }, { start: '2024-01-01', end: '2024-01-02' })` → `2` (2.5 → even).
- `splitByMonth(start, end)`: splits `[start, end)` into segments by calendar month `{ month: 'YYYY-MM', start, end, days }`, in order; the `end` of each segment is day 1 of the following month or the overall `end`. `start === end` → `[]`; `end < start` → `RangeError`.
  - `splitByMonth('2024-01-30', '2024-03-02')` → segments `2024-01` (2 days, up to `2024-02-01`), `2024-02` (29 days), `2024-03` (1 day, up to `2024-03-02`).
- `monthlyCharges(monthlyCents, start, end)`: for each segment of `splitByMonth`, `{ month, days, cents: divRound(monthlyCents × days, daysInMonth(year, month)) }`. E.g.: `monthlyCharges(3100, '2024-01-15', '2024-03-01')` → `[{ month: '2024-01', days: 17, cents: 1700 }, { month: '2024-02', days: 29, cents: 3100 }]`.

## `src/tiers.mjs`

Price table = array of tiers `{ upTo, unitCents, flatCents = 0 }`. `upTo` is the **inclusive** upper limit of the tier (integers ≥ 1, strictly increasing); the last tier — and only it — has `upTo: null` (no limit). Tier `i` covers the quantities `(upTo[i−1], upTo[i]]` (the first one starts at 1). A quantity that is not an integer ≥ 0 → `RangeError`.

- `validateTiers(tiers)`: returns the array itself or throws `RangeError` (empty array, invalid/non-increasing `upTo`, last tier without `null`, non-integer or negative `unitCents`/`flatCents`).
- `tierFor(qty, tiers)`: index of the tier that contains `qty`; `qty = 0` → `-1`.
- `graduated(qty, tiers)`: each unit pays the `unitCents` of the tier it falls in; a tier's `flatCents` is charged once if at least one unit falls in it. → `{ total, breakdown: [{ tier, units, cents }] }`, only tiers with `units > 0`, in order.
- `volume(qty, tiers)`: **all** units pay the `unitCents` of the tier that contains `qty`, plus that tier's `flatCents`. → `{ total, breakdown: [{ tier, units: qty, cents }] }`; `qty = 0` → `{ total: 0, breakdown: [] }`.
- `quote(qty, tiers, mode = 'graduated')`: `'graduated'` or `'volume'`; any other mode → `RangeError`.
- `breakEven(tiers)`: smallest `q ≥ 1` with `volume(q).total < graduated(q).total`, testing `q` from 1 up to the `upTo` of the second-to-last tier + 1 (or only `q = 1` if there is one tier); `null` if there is none.
- With `T = [{ upTo: 100, unitCents: 50 }, { upTo: 1000, unitCents: 40, flatCents: 500 }, { upTo: null, unitCents: 30, flatCents: 1000 }]`: `graduated(101, T)` → `{ total: 5540, breakdown: [{ tier: 0, units: 100, cents: 5000 }, { tier: 1, units: 1, cents: 540 }] }`; `volume(1001, T).total` → `31030`; `tierFor(1000, T)` → `1`.

## `src/tax.mjs`

Tax = `{ code, rateBp, compound = false }`. All roundings are half-even `divRound` of `base × rateBp / 10000`.

- `computeTaxes(nets, taxes, { rounding = 'line' } = {})`: `nets` are net amounts (integers ≥ 0).
  - Groups: with `'line'`, each element of `nets` is a group; with `'invoice'`, there is a single group with the sum of `nets`. The taxes of each group are rounded and then summed by code.
  - In a group with net `N`: each **simple** tax is `round(N × rateBp / 10000)`; each **compound** tax is `round((N + S) × rateBp / 10000)`, where `S` is the sum of the **simple** taxes (already rounded) of the same group — all simple ones, regardless of position in the list. Compound taxes never enter the base of other taxes.
  - → `{ net: Σ nets, byCode: { [code]: cents } (keys in the order of `taxes`), taxTotal, gross: net + taxTotal }`.
  - Empty/duplicate `code`, non-integer or negative `rateBp`, invalid net or unknown `rounding` → `RangeError`.
  - `computeTaxes([1050, 2050], [{ code: 'A', rateBp: 250 }])` → `byCode { A: 77 }` (26 + 51); with `{ rounding: 'invoice' }` → `{ A: 78 }` (77.5 → even).
  - `computeTaxes([10000], [{ code: 'S', rateBp: 500 }, { code: 'C', rateBp: 1000, compound: true }])` → `{ net: 10000, byCode: { S: 500, C: 1050 }, taxTotal: 1550, gross: 11550 }`.
- `extractInclusive(gross, taxes)`: decomposes a price with simple taxes included (any compound → `RangeError`): `base = round(gross × 10000 / (10000 + Σ rateBp))`; each tax `= round(base × rateBp / 10000)`; `net = gross − Σ taxes`. → `{ net, byCode, gross }`. E.g.: `extractInclusive(1100, [{ code: 'A', rateBp: 1000 }])` → `{ net: 1000, byCode: { A: 100 }, gross: 1100 }`.
- `effectiveRateBp({ net, taxTotal })` = `round(taxTotal × 10000 / net)`; `net = 0` → `0`.

## `src/invoice.mjs`

The functions **never change** their arguments (neither the arrays nor the objects inside them); calling twice with the same inputs gives the same result.

- `applyCredits(amount, credits)`: credits `{ id, cents, expires? }` (`cents` integer > 0, otherwise `RangeError`; `amount` integer ≥ 0) are consumed in ascending order of `expires` (`'YYYY-MM-DD'`), credits without `expires` last, ties in input order; each one consumes `min(credit balance, remaining amount)`. → `{ applied: [{ id, cents }] (only uses > 0, in consumption order), unused: [{ id, cents }] (remaining balances > 0, in the same order), remaining }`.
- `buildInvoice(items, { credits = [], minimumCents = 0 } = {})`, items `{ sku, description?, qty, unitCents }` (`sku` non-empty string, `qty` and `unitCents` integers ≥ 0, otherwise `RangeError`):
  1. items with `qty = 0` are ignored; items with the same `sku` **and** the same `unitCents` become a single line, at the position of the first occurrence, with its `description` (`''` if absent) and the summed `qty`. Line = `{ sku, description, qty, unitCents, amount: qty × unitCents }`.
  2. if the subtotal is less than `minimumCents`, appends at the end `{ sku: 'MINIMUM', description: 'Ajuste de consumo mínimo', qty: 1, unitCents: d, amount: d }` with the difference `d`, and the subtotal becomes `minimumCents` (`MINIMUM_SKU` exports `'MINIMUM'`).
  3. applies `applyCredits(subtotal, credits)`.
  - → `{ lines, subtotal, applied, unused, total }` (`total` = remaining amount). `buildInvoice([])` → `{ lines: [], subtotal: 0, applied: [], unused: [], total: 0 }`.
  - E.g.: items `A×7` at 100 with credits `c1` 300 (no expiry), `c2` 200 (`2025-01-31`), `c3` 500 (`2024-12-31`), `c4` 100 (`2024-12-31`) → `applied` `c3:500, c4:100, c2:100`; `unused` `c2:100, c1:300`; `total` `0`.
- `renderInvoice(invoice)`: one line `"<sku> x<qty> <amount>"` per invoice line, then `"CREDIT <id> -<cents>"` per applied credit and finally `"TOTAL <total>"`, joined by `'\n'`, amounts in the format `reais.cents` with two decimal places (`2100` → `21.00`).

bugs.summary: divRound uses Math.trunc instead of Math.floor for the quotient, breaking all modes for negative quotients (negative remainder)
leapsBefore omits the divisibility-by-400 term, shifting all dates from 2001 on by 1 day (intervals crossing 2000→2001 lose a day)
tierFor uses qty < upTo instead of <=, treating the upper limit as exclusive (affects volume and breakEven)
compound taxes accumulate into the base of the following compound ones (simpleSum += amount in the compound loop)
applyCredits copies only the credits array ([...credits]) and debits c.cents on the caller's objects, mutating the input and breaking idempotence
